thread:
Alex: heads-up — having a Dedicated customer (ThermoPay) hit repeated 429s and latency spikes for ~35m, looks like autoscaler is bouncing between +2 and -2 pools. raising an escalation.
Maya: thx. is this the same noisy-batch tenant we saw last month? any repro logs?
Alex: different tenant. I pulled the debug traces. pattern looks like: job bursts -> scale up -> warmup cache and prefetch saturates memory -> token-latency jumps -> clients retry -> autoscaler reads higher util -> scales up again -> then traffic drops and it scales down quickly. repeat.
Raj: can you paste the relevant timeline + metrics? curious what metric triggers scale (cpu? queued-reqs?)
Alex: autoscaler uses request-rate (per-pool qps) with 60s window and cooldown 45s. here's the window around the bounce (timestamps are relative):
```
00:00 incoming qps spike to 220 (baseline 40)
00:30 scaled +2 nodes (30s deployment)
01:10 p50 token latency -> 900ms (was 75ms)
01:20 clients retry, qps jumps to 350
01:45 autoscaler observes sustained qps -> scale +1
02:10 traffic falls to 30, cooldown expired -> scale -3
02:40 repeat
```
Maya: that 45s cooldown is too short given our warmup + deploy time. warmup causes transient amplified load from retries.
Luke: also see KV-cache thrash in the logs at 01:10 — cold cache population causing heavy GPU mem usage for a minute.
Alex: attached a sample error payload from the customer: 429s with body {"code":"throttled","retry_after":1} and a client that immediately retries up to 3x.
Raj: so causes are: short cooldown, retry storm, warmup memory spike from large batch jobs. any auth or billing errors tied in?
Alex: billing looks normal. auth refreshes for that tenant were fine. it's service-level throttles causing SRE paging.
autoscale-bot: detected rapid scale events: events=[+2,+1,-3,+2] interval=35m. anomaly score=0.87 :eyes:
Maya: quick mitigation options:
- increase cooldown to 180s
- use moving-average smoothing on qps (3-min)
- per-tenant concurrency cap so one tenant can't occupy >40% of a pool
- backend: enable pre-warmed KV shards for heavy tenants
Luke: for immediate customer relief we can pin them to an isolated dedicated pool (manual) and set their max-instances=6 and burst-protection on.
Raj: agree. also add a retry-backoff header enforcement (min retry-after 3s) so clients don't amplify.
Alex: repro steps I'm running locally (dev cluster):
1) spin up dedicated pool with same config
2) run synthetic job that sends 2x burst every 60s with client retry=3 immediate
3) capture autoscaler decisions and kernel mem usage
logs snippet:
```
2026-03-15T01:09:58Z pool-a: qps=215 cpu=72% gpu_mem=68% kv_miss=0.87
2026-03-15T01:10:20Z pool-a: scale_event start scale_delta=2 reason=request_rate
2026-03-15T01:11:15Z pool-a: client_retries spike=180
2026-03-15T01:11:45Z pool-a: p50_token_latency=912ms
```
Maya: can we push a temp rule to increase cooldown + smoothing for the affected pool and notify customer team? that's lowest-risk.
Alex: i'll open the tenant isolation task and do the cooldown change now. will follow up with reproduction artifact + perf graphs.
Raj: create a quick runbook snippet for oncall: how to pin tenant, adjust cooldown, and check kv-warmup. include commands.
Luke: noted — I'll prepare the commands, also add an alert for "scale-flap-rate" that triggers at >3 scale events in 15m.
Alex: thanks. tagging @customer-support to notify ThermoPay. Maya i'll ping you when I push the cooldown rule.
Maya: ack. also recommend we add a changelog note: "autoscaler cooldown default increased to 120s for pools with large-workload tenants" if this becomes product-level change.
Alex: update: cooldown bumped to 180s on the pool and we've pinned the tenant to isolated pool. initial 10m looked stable, no new 429s. I'll leave thread open for 1h for monitoring.
Raj: great. please paste the dashboard link when ready and file a short postmortem if it doesn't stabilize.
Alex: dashboard https://redwood.internal/dashboards/pool-a/3176549876 — monitoring.
autoscale-bot: monitoring rule: scale-flap-rate=0 -> 1 after cooldown change
